g.text: Self-adaptive large language models (LLMs) would represent a significant
advancement in artificial intelligence, providing a framework where models
can adjust to varied tasks and dynamic contexts in real time.
g.title: N1 [Context] (cites=0) Self-adaptive large language models (LLMs) would represent a significant advancement in artificial intelligence, providing a framework where models can adjust to varied tasks and dynamic contexts in real time.

g.text: This concept draws inspiration from the long-standing idea of
neural networks modifying their own weights to adapt to tasks
dynamically (Schmidhuber, 1993; Irie et al., 2022) and neural
networks generating weights for other networks, as…
g.title: N2 [Prior_Work] (cites=4) This concept draws inspiration from the long-standing idea of neural networks modifying their own weights to adapt to tasks dynamically (Schmidhuber, 1993; Irie et al., 2022) and neural networks generating weights for other networks, as popularized by HyperNetworks and related methods (Ha et al., 2017; Stanley et al., 2009).

g.text: Current LLM training lacks both compositionality +
While compositionality and scalability are crucial for effective
adaptation, current LLM training methodologies fall short of
g.title: N3 [Limitation] (cites=0) While compositionality and scalability are crucial for effective adaptation, current LLM training methodologies fall short of achieving both these properties simultaneously.

g.text: Our research aims to present a pioneering solution to realize this
g.title: N4 [Method] (cites=0) Our research aims to present a pioneering solution to realize this vision.

g.text: Traditionally, LLM post-training has sought to optimize a model
for a wide range of capabilities in a single, extensive training
g.title: N5 [Prior_Work] (cites=0) Traditionally, LLM post-training has sought to optimize a model for a wide range of capabilities in a single, extensive training session.

g.text: One-shot ideal but hard in practice
While this “one-shot” fine-tuning framework is ideal from a
simplicity perspective, it is also difficult to achieve in
g.title: N6 [Limitation] (cites=0) While this “one-shot” fine-tuning framework is ideal from a simplicity perspective, it is also difficult to achieve in practice.

g.text: For instance, post-training is still highly
g.title: N7 [Limitation] (cites=0) For instance, post-training is still highly resource-intensive, leading to significant computational costs and training times.

g.text: Additionally, there tends to be notable performance trade-offs
when introducing additional breadth to the data, making it
challenging to overcome overfitting and task interference at the
g.title: N8 [Limitation] (cites=0) Additionally, there tends to be notable performance trade-offs when introducing additional breadth to the data, making it challenging to overcome overfitting and task interference at the same time.

g.text: In contrast, self-adaptive models offer a more flexible and
efficient approach. Rather than attempting to train an LLM for all
tasks in one step, expert modules can be developed offline and
augmented to the base LLM on-demand (Kang et al.,…
g.title: N9 [Prior_Work] (cites=1) In contrast, self-adaptive models offer a more flexible and efficient approach. Rather than attempting to train an LLM for all tasks in one step, expert modules can be developed offline and augmented to the base LLM on-demand (Kang et al., 2024).

g.text: This allows the model to dynamically modify its behavior based on the task
at hand, without the need for constant re-tuning.
g.title: N10 [Prior_Work] (cites=0) This allows the model to dynamically modify its behavior based on the task at hand, without the need for constant re-tuning.

g.text: In addition to the benefit of having independent components, this modularity
also supports continual learning, enabling the model to add new skills over
g.title: N11 [Prior_Work] (cites=0) In addition to the benefit of having independent components, this modularity also supports continual learning, enabling the model to add new skills over time without catastrophic forgetting.

g.text: Moreover, self-adaptive LLMs mirror a well-established principle in
neuroscience and computational biology, where the brain activates specific
regions depending on the task at hand (Loose et al., 2017) and dynamically
g.title: N12 [Prior_Work] (cites=2) Moreover, self-adaptive LLMs mirror a well-established principle in neuroscience and computational biology, where the brain activates specific regions depending on the task at hand (Loose et al., 2017) and dynamically reconfigures its functional networks in response to changing task demands (Davison et al., 2015).

g.text: In principle, the first step toward achieving self-adaptive LLMs can be
realized through the development of specialized expert modules, each
fine-tuned (Kaplan et al., 2020) via techniques such as low-rank adaptation
g.title: N13 [Prior_Work] (cites=2) In principle, the first step toward achieving self-adaptive LLMs can be realized through the development of specialized expert modules, each fine-tuned (Kaplan et al., 2020) via techniques such as low-rank adaptation (LoRA) (Hu et al., 2021).

g.text: These expert modules can then be dynamically composed at runtime based on
the task demands, a process that can be efficiently managed through Mixture
g.title: N14 [Prior_Work] (cites=1) These expert modules can then be dynamically composed at runtime based on the task demands, a process that can be efficiently managed through Mixture of Experts (MoE)-like systems (Tianlong et al., 2024).

g.text: However, several challenges need to be addressed to make this
g.title: N15 [Limitation] (cites=0) However, several challenges need to be addressed to make this approach both scalable and compositional.

g.text: First, fine-tuning LLMs to create multiple expert
modules significantly increases the number of
parameters that need to be trained.
g.title: N15a [Limitation: challenge-1] (cites=0) First, fine-tuning LLMs to create multiple expert modules significantly increases the number of parameters that need to be trained.

g.text: In practice, even with parameter-efficient methods like LoRA, the
cumulative size of these modules can quickly escalate, leading to
g.title: N15b [Limitation] (cites=0) In practice, even with parameter-efficient methods like LoRA, the cumulative size of these modules can quickly escalate, leading to increased storage and computational demands.

g.text: Second, these expert modules are often prone to
overfitting, a phenomenon especially prevalent when
training on smaller datasets or narrow task domains.
g.title: N15c [Limitation: challenge-2] (cites=0) Second, these expert modules are often prone to overfitting, a phenomenon especially prevalent when training on smaller datasets or narrow task domains.

g.text: Third, the flexible composition of these expert modules
also presents largely unresolved challenges currently
g.title: N15d [Limitation: challenge-3] (cites=0) Third, the flexible composition of these expert modules also presents largely unresolved challenges currently posing as open research problems.

g.text: To overcome these limitations, we first propose Singular Value
method to obtain effective building blocks for self-adaptation.
g.title: N16 [Method] (cites=0) To overcome these limitations, we first propose Singular Value Fine-tuning (SVF), a novel parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) method to obtain effective building blocks for self-adaptation.

g.text: SVF works by extracting and tuning only the singular values within the
g.title: N17 [Method] (cites=0) SVF works by extracting and tuning only the singular values within the model's weight matrices.

g.text: By focusing on this principled parameterization, our approach mitigates the
risk of overfitting, drastically reduces computational demands, and allows
g.title: N18 [Method] (cites=0) By focusing on this principled parameterization, our approach mitigates the risk of overfitting, drastically reduces computational demands, and allows for inherent compositionality.

g.text: We show these properties enable us to cheaply obtain a set of effective
domain-specific “expert” vectors by training on narrow datasets with RL,
directly optimizing task performance on individual topics.
g.title: N19 [Method] (cites=0) We show these properties enable us to cheaply obtain a set of effective domain-specific “expert” vectors by training on narrow datasets with RL, directly optimizing task performance on individual topics.

g.text: We then introduce our full Transformer2 (Transformer-Squared) framework to
empower LLMs through the underlying principles of self-adaptation.
g.title: N20 [Method] (cites=0) We then introduce our full Transformer2 (Transformer-Squared) framework to empower LLMs through the underlying principles of self-adaptation.

g.text: Given a prompt from an unknown task, Transformer2 entails a two-pass
inference mechanism which we illustrate in Figure 1.
g.title: N21 [Method] (cites=0) Given a prompt from an unknown task, Transformer2 entails a two-pass inference mechanism which we illustrate in Figure 1.

g.text: During the first pass, Transformer2 executes the model and observes its
test-time behavior, gathering the relevant information to understand the
necessary skills to tackle the current problem.
g.title: N22 [Method] (cites=0) During the first pass, Transformer2 executes the model and observes its test-time behavior, gathering the relevant information to understand the necessary skills to tackle the current problem.

g.text: During the second pass, our framework uses this information to combine the
available expert vectors and provide a new modification to the base weights
of the LLM specifically tailored to its test-time conditions.
g.title: N23 [Method] (cites=0) During the second pass, our framework uses this information to combine the available expert vectors and provide a new modification to the base weights of the LLM specifically tailored to its test-time conditions.

g.text: We design three different adaptation strategies that can be used within
Transformer2, which we show provide monotonic performance benefits with
increasing access to the test-time conditions.
g.title: N24 [Method] (cites=0) We design three different adaptation strategies that can be used within Transformer2, which we show provide monotonic performance benefits with increasing access to the test-time conditions.

g.text: We evaluate SVF and the full Transformer2 framework through extensive
experiments across a diverse range of LLMs and tasks.
g.title: N25 [Result] (cites=0) We evaluate SVF and the full Transformer2 framework through extensive experiments across a diverse range of LLMs and tasks.

g.text: SVF beats LoRA with far fewer params
First, when trained on domain-specific datasets, we show that SVF
consistently outperforms traditional strategies for efficient fine-tuning
such as LoRA, and at the same time, with orders of magnitudes fewer
g.title: N26 [Result] (cites=0) First, when trained on domain-specific datasets, we show that SVF consistently outperforms traditional strategies for efficient fine-tuning such as LoRA, and at the same time, with orders of magnitudes fewer parameters.

g.text: Transformer2 adapts even on VQA OOD
Then we show that Transformer2 is able to push performance far further,
effectively adapting the weights of the base model even in entirely
out-of-distribution applications such as visual question answering.
g.title: N27 [Result] (cites=0) Then we show that Transformer2 is able to push performance far further, effectively adapting the weights of the base model even in entirely out-of-distribution applications such as visual question answering.

g.text: Finally, we analyze the properties of our new framework, validating that it
provides increasing benefits with additional access to its current test-time
conditions and even allow for recycling pre-trained SVF experts across
g.title: N28 [Result] (cites=0) Finally, we analyze the properties of our new framework, validating that it provides increasing benefits with additional access to its current test-time conditions and even allow for recycling pre-trained SVF experts across model architectures.

g.text: The development of Transformer2 as a pivotal self-adaptation
framework for LLMs, providing a universal blueprint to dynamically
adapt the behavior of LLMs from a growing set of pre-trained
g.title: C1 [Contribution] (cites=0) The development of Transformer2 as a pivotal self-adaptation framework for LLMs, providing a universal blueprint to dynamically adapt the behavior of LLMs from a growing set of pre-trained skills.

g.text: C2: SVF PEFT method via RL
The introduction of SVF, a novel PEFT method trainable with RL on
small datasets, producing compact expert vectors with inherent
compositionality, all key properties necessary for our scalable
g.title: C2 [Contribution] (cites=0) The introduction of SVF, a novel PEFT method trainable with RL on small datasets, producing compact expert vectors with inherent compositionality, all key properties necessary for our scalable self-adaptation framework.

g.text: The implementation of three adaptation strategies within
Transformer2, effectively dispatching SVF-trained experts with
properties designed to cope with different requirements and
g.title: C3 [Contribution] (cites=0) The implementation of three adaptation strategies within Transformer2, effectively dispatching SVF-trained experts with properties designed to cope with different requirements and deployment scenarios.
